files.release-scope.md: Consumer: iOS field app. Baseline: 1.3. Target: 1.4. Business behavior: an assigned technician submits one completion report for an open work order. Changed operation: POST /v1/reports. Required header: Idempotency-Key, string, unique per submission. Request JSON fields: workOrderId string required; completedAt RFC 3339 string required; latitude number required from -90 through 90; longitude number required from -180 through 180. Success: HTTP 201 with reportId string and status ACCEPTED. Special error: HTTP 422, code INVALID_GPS, when coordinates are outside the allowed range; show the coordinate error and do not retry unchanged input. Special error: HTTP 409, code WORK_ORDER_CLOSED, when a supervisor already closed the work order; preserve the draft, refresh the work order, and do not retry automatically. Compatibility: additive operation, iOS 1.3 remains supported; iOS 1.4 must add the submission flow. Internal detail to exclude: ReportRepository now writes through CompletionReportService and an outbox table. Unchanged and out of scope: GET /v1/users. Admin-only and out of scope: POST /v1/admin/reports.

files.data-contract.md: The approved concept is WorkOrder. API requests and events call its identifier workOrderId. PostgreSQL uses snake_case, so named columns and foreign keys use work_order_id consistently. The WorkOrder table may retain the established table-local primary key id, but the database handoff must show its mapping to workOrderId. Each work order belongs to one tenant and has a tenant-unique external reference. A CompletionReport belongs to exactly one WorkOrder and may be accepted only once. Retries carry an idempotency key unique per tenant for 30 days. Supervisors can close open work orders concurrently with technician submission, which must return a conflict rather than overwrite. Primary reads: paginated assigned open work orders ordered by due_at and lookup by tenant plus external reference. Reports are retained seven years.
